title: Crestwood Clinics - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for onboarding Crestwood Clinics onto Redwood. Covered success criteria (latency <250ms for sync tasks, P95 throughput targets, HIPAA constraints), deployment options (private VPC vs Dedicated), timelines for pilot and production, required security documentation. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing & pilot plan, SE to run small benchmark, customer to share network diagrams and sample anonymized dataset.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-06-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Dr. Ellen Park (CTO, Crestwood), Samira Khan (Head of Data), Tom Rivera (IT)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff to align on pilot scope, security checkpoints, and initial timeline. Some audio dropouts around 00:22:00.

00:00:05 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, excited to kick this off. Can folks quick intro?
00:00:12 - Dr. Ellen Park: Hi, Ellen here, I'm CTO at Crestwood Clinics. We're looking to embed Redwood for patient triage and clinician note summarization.
00:00:20 - Samira Khan: Samira, Head of Data. I'll own dataset prep and evaluation.
00:00:25 - Tom Rivera: Tom, IT manager. I'll handle network and infra requirements.
00:00:30 - Maya: Great, from Redwood we have Arjun SE for technical, Luis our CSM.
00:00:38 - Arjun: Hey all. Quick note on call plan: we'll review success criteria, deployment options, security, then pilot timeline.

00:01:10 - Samira: For success metrics we care about latency, specifically p95 under 250 milliseconds for the sync flows, and throughput to handle our daily peak which is about 800 concurrent sessions, and of course accuracy on note summaries - we have internal eval sets.
00:01:30 - Maya: Perfect, that'll help scope Dedicated vs Private. Quick question — are you allowed to host patient data outside your VPC?
00:01:40 - Dr. Ellen Park: Short answer, no. We need either private deployment inside our cloud account or Redwood Dedicated with strong data isolation and signed BAAs. HIPAA is a requirement.
00:01:55 - Luis: We do offer Private deployments and Dedicated clusters plus BAAs. We'll surface SOC2/ISO docs as well.

00:02:20 - Tom: From an IT side, we use AWS in us-east-1, have strict egress controls, we use SAML SSO via Okta, and we have an internal proxy for outbound calls. We'll need network instructions.
00:02:35 - Arjun: Noted. For Private we can do a customer-managed VPC peering or Transit Gateway integration. For Dedicated, we can provide isolated GPU pools and ingestion doesn't leave Redwood's managed infra — though we need to confirm retention policies per the BAAs.

00:03:05 - Samira: On dataset — we can provide an anonymized set of 500 clinical notes and a set of prompts for summarization. Want to make sure benchmarking is apples-to-apples.
00:03:18 - Arjun: That works. We'll run two variants: an open LLM we recommend + a quantized variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll capture P50/P95 latencies, tokens/sec, and token cost estimates.

00:04:00 - Dr. Ellen Park: One of our concerns is cold start latency and session affinity when clinicians open patient records. Any suggestions?
00:04:12 - Arjun: We recommend prefix caching for repeat prompts, and warm pools for Dedicated. For Private, cache configuration happens in the runtime. We'll share recommended cache TTLs.

00:04:40 - Samira: Also, how does Redwood handle audit logs and ability to export logs for audits?
00:04:50 - Luis: We provide audit logs for inference requests, model versions, and admin actions. They can be exported to S3 or streamed to your SIEM. We'll include sample schemas.

00:05:10 - Tom: Ok, on networking — do you require static egress IPs for Dedicated? We need that for firewall rules.
00:05:18 - Arjun: For Dedicated we can provide static egress IP ranges. For Private inside your VPC, egress is under your control. We'll send the required IP ranges and ports.

00:06:00 - Maya: On timelines, what are you thinking for pilot window and go-live?
00:06:05 - Dr. Ellen Park: Ideally pilot in 3 weeks, production in 8-10 weeks if pilot is good. Security review will be the gating item.
00:06:15 - Luis: That's doable. Pilot scope: 2-week limited pilot with up to 50 clinicians, run benchmarks, validate quality/regressions, security assessment.

00:06:40 - Samira: We'll need a clear rollback plan if quality regresses after a model update, and ability to pin model versions.
00:06:48 - Arjun: Redwood supports version pinning and rollouts (canary/A-B) plus automatic fallback policies. We can demo that in the next technical deep dive.

00:07:20 - Dr. Ellen Park: Pricing — we need per-token and also evaluation of committed capacity.
00:07:28 - Maya: I'll send a detailed pricing sheet with hosted per-token, Dedicated committed capacity options and an estimated cost for the pilot.
00:07:35 - Samira: Any compliance questionnaire we should fill out?
00:07:40 - Luis: Yes, we have a standard security questionnaire and SOC2 report. We'll attach those to the email.

00:08:05 - Tom: One more — we run strict data retention for logs. Can Redwood configure retention windows?
00:08:12 - Luis: Yes — retention windows are configurable for Private. For Dedicated we'll align retention with contract terms; we can add shorter retention for logs and enable automatic purging.

00:08:40 - Speaker 1: (small audio dropout) sorry, could you repeat that?
00:08:44 - Arjun: Sure — on rate limits, we'll set per-tenant quotas and token limits during the pilot and can increase as needed.

00:09:05 - Samira: For the benchmark, can we get a simple CSV with per-request latency and outputs so we can run our own eval scripts?
00:09:12 - Arjun: Absolutely. We'll provide the raw request/response logs in a sanitized CSV.

00:09:35 - Dr. Ellen Park: Are there restrictions around model fine-tuning? We may want a small supervised finetune for summarization.
00:09:44 - Maya: We support both fine-tuning workflows and fine-tune-like approaches (in-context tuning / RLHF depending on model). For Private or Dedicated we can enable training pipelines, but that has extra considerations — we can go into details in the SE deep dive.

00:10:05 - Tom: Ok, next steps?
00:10:10 - Luis: I'll create the onboarding calendar and set weekly check-ins.
00:10:15 - Maya: I'll email pricing, pilot scope, and security docs by Thursday.
00:10:20 - Arjun: I'll run the benchmark once Samira sends the anonymized sample by Monday.
00:10:26 - Samira: Sending sample by Sunday evening.
00:10:30 - Dr. Ellen Park: Great.

00:10:45 - Maya: Anything else from Crestwood?
00:10:50 - Tom: We'll confirm the Okta admin and share the network diagram.
00:10:55 - Samira: No, that's it. Looking forward.

00:11:05 - Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the notes and action items. Talk soon.

(End of recording with a few short crosstalk moments and one small audio dropout around 00:08:40.)
